summary: Winston County, AL 79-foot pressure-treated wood tower site registered in 2017; Alabama Forestry Commission records say the site is reclaimed with no trace of the tower left.

facts.status_note: Register says the site has been reclaimed and no trace of the tower exists today

events.note: Registered April 24, 2017 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register; nominated by Andrew Zerbe

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
79-foot tower made of pressure-treated wood, per Alabama Forestry Commission records
evidence.quote: Alabama Forestry Commission records say this was a 79' tower made of pressure treated wood.

evidence.supports: site reclaimed and no trace of the tower exists today
evidence.quote: The site has been reclaimed and no trace of it exists today.
over 200 of these artifacts dotted Alabama

evidence.supports: aircraft as the most common explanation for decline; planes covered a broader area than a 100-foot tower
evidence.quote: The most common explanation is that aircraft was more efficient in spotting fires in a much broader area than a 100-foot tower could provide.

evidence.supports: Alabama retains about a third of the lookouts it once had
evidence.quote: Today, Alabama retains only about a third of the lookouts it once had.

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Only the Former Fire Lookout Sites page describes this tower; its design and reclamation statements are attributed to Alabama Forestry Commission records. The Kaufmann column (source 2) is general context about Alabama towers, not about this site. Two web searches gave no build date, staffing or fire history, so none is written. Access is not established by any source. The NHLR URL guessed at nhlr.org/lookouts/us/al/lockhart-alabama-3-lookout-site/ returned 404 in the crawl cache; that does not prove the site is absent from NHLR.
